n_participants: 522 (Stroop/Simon files in Complete_02-16-2019; Discovery=200, Validation=300, plus separate Retest_02-16-2019 sample -- varies slightly per task)
n_items: ~50-90k trials per task per sample (trial-level; e.g. stroop.csv.gz has 50112 test-stage rows across 522 workers)
contributors: A. Zeynep Enkavi; Ian W. Eisenberg; Patrick G. Bissett; Gina L. Mazza; David P. MacKinnon; Lisa A. Marsch; Russell A. Poldrack
contributor_profiles: https://github.com/IanEisenberg; https://github.com/zenkavi (analysis repo owner, likely corresponding contact)
contributor_email: zenkavi@stanford.edu (A. Zeynep Enkavi, found directly in the PMC article page, PMC6431228)
notes: User-directed lead (2026-07-17), not from automated discovery -- user pointed directly at the PNAS paper's data-availability link. Exceptional match for the conflict-task/reliability-paradox vignette: this IS a test-retest reliability paper on self-regulation tasks. The Individual_Measures folder (checked in both Data/Complete_02-16-2019 and Data/Retest_02-16-2019) has genuine trial-level long-format CSVs for essentially the whole target paradigm family in one battery -- stroop.csv.gz, simon.csv.gz, attention_network_task.csv.gz (flanker component), go_nogo.csv.gz, stop_signal.csv.gz, motor_selective_stop_signal.csv.gz, stim_selective_stop_signal.csv.gz, local_global_letter.csv.gz (Navon/global-local), dot_pattern_expectancy.csv.gz (AX-CPT variant), threebytwo.csv.gz + shift_task.csv.gz (task-switching) -- each with a matching Retest-sample file, i.e. this dataset could support the reliability analysis directly rather than only the group-effect side. Confirmed structure by downloading stroop/simon/attention_network_task.csv.gz directly: columns include worker_id (person id), trial_id, condition (congruent/incongruent), correct, rt, exp_stage (test/practice -- filter to test) -- would map cleanly to id/item/resp/cov_condition per datastandard.md. BLOCKED ON LICENSE: no LICENSE file on the GitHub repo (checked via API + raw file probes for LICENSE/LICENSE.md/LICENSE.txt/license, all 404), no license field on the repo itself, and no OSF companion project found. NIH-funded (Science of Behavior Change Common Fund, NIDA UH2DA041713) and clearly intended for reuse given the detailed public data release, but intent is not the same as an explicit license -- GitHub's own policy is that no LICENSE file defaults to all-rights-reserved. Strong candidate for an author-permission email; zenkavi@stanford.edu found directly in PMC metadata (not guessed). UPDATE 2026-07-17: author permission confirmed, released under CC BY. data/enkavi_2019_conflict_tasks.py processes 8 conflict-task tables (stroop, simon, ant_flanker, gonogo, dpx_axcpt, navon, stopsignal, taskswitch) with wave=1/2 for Complete/Retest samples -- output in irw_output/, tags/dictionary entries and Redivis upload still pending.
